newsitem.title: USA: Nov emerging markets bond index up 4.99 pct - Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Nov emerging markets bond index up 4.99 pct - Morgan.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc's Emerging Markets Bond Index Plus (EMBI+) rose 4.99 percent in November, bringing its year-to-date return to 37.66 percent, according to a J.P. Morgan report.
All 14 countries in the index gained last month.
"The renewed emerging markets rally was driven by investors' favorable reaction to the U.S. election results and the (Federal Reserve's) decision not to raise interest rates," the report said.
Bulgarian debt instruments rose 12.02 percent last month, making Bulgaria the best-performing market in the index.
Increased likelihood of an International Monetary Fund-financed currency board created much of the positive sentiment, it said.

South Africa turned in the worst November performance, rising 1.5 percent. "The short duration and tight spread on its debt limit the potential for high returns," the report said. South African returns are 8.75 percent so far in 1996 and lag behind the other countries in the index.
Russia leads the EMBI+ on a year-to-date basis, with returns of 110.97 percent.

The Emerging Markets Bond Index Plus tracks total returns for traded external debt instruments, including Brady bonds, loans and Eurobonds, as well as U.S. dollar local market instruments in emerging markets.
Additionally, J.P. Morgan said its Emerging Local Markets Index (ELMI) rose 1.49 percent in November and 13.66 percent year-to-date.
Mexico rose 4.65 percent last month to lead the ELMI, while Turkey declined 0.65 percent for last place.
The ELMI tracks total returns for local-denominated money market instruments.
